name: Clang / LLVM
description: C/C++/Objective-C compiler. The NDK ships its own clang; Termux ships a native clang that targets Android bionic.
requirements: C++17 or newer for modern engines
limitations: NDK clang and host clang are separate installations
libstdc++ is not the Android default
Some sanitizers are unavailable on Android

name: GCC
description: GNU Compiler Collection. Useful for host-side tools and for building dependencies, but Android targets require the NDK clang toolchain.
limitations: Not the supported Android compiler
ABI differences from libc++
Cross-compiling to bionic with GCC is unsupported

name: CMake
description: Cross-platform build system generator. Android builds use the NDK toolchain file and the Ninja generator.
limitations: CMake 4.x removed compatibility with some old projects that set cmake_minimum_required below 3.5
Toolchain file path changes between NDK releases

name: Ninja
description: Small, fast build executor used by CMake and the Android Gradle Plugin for native builds.
limitations: Not a build system by itself
Poor diagnostics compared with Make for hand-written rules

name: NDK CMake toolchain
description: The android.toolchain.cmake file shipped with the NDK. Configures clang, sysroot, ABI, STL and API level for cross-compilation.
limitations: Requires the full NDK, not just ndk-sysroot
Variables differ slightly across NDK majors

name: SDL2
description: Cross-platform windowing, input, audio and file abstraction. Has a first-class Android backend driven by NativeActivity.
requirements: SDL main activity in the manifest
AAssetManager passed to SDL_main or the SDL hint set
limitations: SDL2 is in maintenance while SDL3 develops
Desktop-specific hints do not apply on Android
Touch events need mapping to game input

name: SDL3
description: The next major SDL release with a revised API, GPU abstraction and improved Android support.
limitations: API differs substantially from SDL2
Ecosystem support is still growing
Some backends are newer and less battle-tested

name: GLFW
description: Small desktop windowing library for OpenGL/Vulkan contexts. No official Android backend; mobile ports require a replacement or a custom shell.
requirements: Desktop window system (X11, Wayland, Cocoa, Win32)
limitations: No Android support upstream
Must be replaced with SDL, android-activity or a custom EGL shell

name: Dear ImGui
description: Immediate-mode GUI for tools, debug overlays and game menus. Renders through a backend (OpenGL, Vulkan, SDL_GPU) and works on Android with touch input.
requirements: Input backend mapping touch to mouse events
limitations: Not a retained-mode UI toolkit
Font atlas must be sized for high-DPI screens
Touch targets need explicit sizing

name: EnTT
description: Header-only entity-component-system library used by many C++ games for gameplay object storage.
limitations: No serialization or networking built in
Registry lifetime is the app's responsibility

name: GLM
description: Header-only C++ mathematics library matching GLSL conventions. Vectors, matrices, quaternions and transforms.
limitations: Column-major by default; Vulkan clip-space adjustments are manual
No SIMD guarantee

name: Assimp
description: Asset import library for dozens of 3D model formats. Useful for converting desktop game assets into an engine-specific format.
requirements: CMake build for the target ABI
limitations: Large binary size
Not a runtime loader for every format
Some importers are incomplete

name: miniaudio
description: Single-header audio playback and capture library with AAudio, OpenSL ES and other backends. Small and dependency-free.
requirements: One header plus one implementation TU
Backend selected at compile time or runtime
limitations: No high-level mixing graph
Streaming large files needs a custom data source

name: Vulkan SDK
description: LunarG SDK with Vulkan headers, loader, validation layers and shader tools. The NDK provides its own Vulkan headers for Android builds.
requirements: Desktop host for the full SDK
NDK Vulkan headers for Android target builds
limitations: SDK tools are host binaries, not Android binaries
Validation layers are desktop-only in practice
glslc/dxc output must match the target's capabilities

name: OpenAL Soft
description: Cross-platform 3D audio library implementing the OpenAL API, with an Android backend.
requirements: CMake build for the target ABI
limitations: Larger than miniaudio
3D positional audio quality depends on HRTF configuration
Backend selection needs testing per device
